items.item_text: Certification as a Clinical Research Associate or Coordinator.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Occasional evenings and weekends may be required. Position is fully onsite.
Theoretical knowledge of biology, microbiology, clinical sciences as typically attained by a Bachelor's degree, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience performing clinical research duties in a clinical research environment.
A minimum of one year of experience performing clinical research duties in a clinical research environment.

Experience using statistical software applications. Knowledge of database, word processing, and spreadsheet applications. This includes the Microsoft Office suite, REDCap, Matlab, and R Statistical programming, or a similar software.
Proven experience in the UC San Diego Health Sciences environment.
Experience following laboratory Standard Operating Procedures.
Experience with research audits.
Experience with the application of inclusion and exclusion criteria.
Experience with clinical trials participant or study subject recruitment.
Experience interpreting medical charts, and abstracting data from medical records.
Experience coordinating study startup activities.
Experience completing case report forms.
Experience providing in-service training to various research personnel on protocols, processes, and procedures.
Experience maintaining files and keeping records.
Experience working with research bulk accounts within Velos or a similar system.

Under the supervision of the Principal Investigator (PI) and lab manager, the incumbent will independently support the research and clinical efforts of the Women's Imaging Lab in the Department of Radiology.

The incumbent will be able to independently coordinate and perform a wide variety of standard operating procedures in all phases of pre-clinical, translational, and clinical research. This includes experimental procedures, patient recruitment, screening, enrollment, scheduling in collaboration with clinics, data collection, and performing all responsibilities according to the principles of GCP. The incumbent will maintain organized records pertinent to each research protocol, including correspondence with collaborative organizations and groups. They will adhere to federal, state, and University regulations and guidelines of personal health information and maintenance of de-identified data collection. They will assist the lab manager with Institutional Review Board (IRB) protocol submission, revision, and updates. They will provide assistance to scientists, clinicans, lab postdocs, and visiting scholars in their research.

Written communication is central to this role. The incumbent will directly communicate with assigned physicians and research groups, attend weekly meetings and tumor boards, provide direct assistance to the PI and Lab Manager in reviewing and verifying university policies, research account statements, and in coordinating subject accrual with referring physicians and imaging facility personnel.
While not required, a cover letter is highly recommended when applying to this position.
Fluency in Spanish.
MRI Safety Trained.

Excellent interpersonal, as well as written and verbal communication skills (using grammatically correct written English and accurate typing) to interact with a diverse population. Excellent phone etiquette skills.

Knowledge of policy and procedure in the following domains: National Institute of Health (NIH), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP), Office of IRB Administration (OIA), IATA Shipping of Blood Specimens, and Bloodborne Pathogens.
Excellent planning and organizational skills and ability to work in a changing, multiple-demand setting in order to prioritize a large volume of work and meet deadlines efficiently and accurately.
Knowledge of MRI physics and processes
Ability to work independently. Ability to maintain confidentiality.
Demonstrated ability to interact effectively with diverse groups, including professional and non-professional staff and research participants.
